newsitem.title: CHINA: China 1996 natural disasters affect 300 million.
newsitem.headline: China 1996 natural disasters affect 300 million.

text.p: Earthquakes, a drought in north China and floods in central and southern provinces affected 300 million people and left 40 million with difficulty finding food, clothing or shelter, newspapers said on Saturday.
A total of 26 earthquakes measuring more than 5.0 on the Richter scale were recorded in 1996, the People's Daily and the China Daily said, quoting Vice-Minister of Civil Affairs Fan Baojun.
Other major natural disasters in 1996 included a drought in north China, summer floods in central and southern provinces, snowstorms and typhoons, the newspapers said.
The newspapers did not say how many people were killed or injured in the natural disasters or give an estimate of damage caused to property. They also did not give comparative figures.
Fan was quoted as saying the disasters affected about 300 million people and about 40 million had difficulty finding food, clothing or shelter.
Relief for disaster victims totalled a record six billion yuan ($723 million), the newspapers said.
Of the figure, 2.3 billion yuan ($277 million) came from the central government and 1.45 billion ($175 million) from local governments, they said.
Urban residents across China, foreign governments, international organisations and residents of Hong Kong and Taiwan donated the rest, the newspapers said.
Relief supplies included large quantities of food, clothing, blankets and medicine, Fan said.

Food was distributed to more than 40 million people, 12.6 million people were given clothing and blankets, 4.3 million received medical care and more than five million homeless people were resettled, the newspapers said.
Four million new dwellings were built with government aid, the vice-minister said.
